Zoe's teacher gave the class a challenge: go one whole week without your phone.
Zoe thought it would be a piece of cake. By the end of day one, she'd reached for her phone about fifty times.
On day two, she was so bored that she actually picked up a book her aunt had given her.
She ended up reading half of it in one night.
By day four, she'd noticed something weird: she was falling asleep faster and wasn't as tired in the morning.
She also talked to her parents at dinner way more than usual. Her dad even taught her how to play chess.
When the week was over, she got her phone back.
She still uses it, but now she leaves it in the kitchen at night.

Ethan tried to make small talk, but it was pretty awkward.
Then he noticed an old photo on the table — a young man in a baseball uniform.
"Is that you?" Ethan asked. Mr. Alvarez's face lit up.
It turned out he'd played in the minor leagues back in the fifties, and he had tons of crazy stories.
Ethan ended up staying two hours longer than he had to.
He finished his required hours months ago, but he still visits every Saturday.
Looking back, he says it was a blessing in disguise that he needed those hours in the first place.

Hey everyone, welcome back to the show. Today we're talking about something we all do: procrastination.
Here's the thing — most people think procrastination is about being lazy. But researchers say that's not really it.
It's actually more about managing emotions. When a task makes us feel anxious, bored, or overwhelmed, we put it off to feel better right now.
The problem is, that relief is temporary. The task is still there, and now we feel guilty on top of it.
So what actually helps? One strategy is to make the first step ridiculously small. Instead of "write my essay," try "write one sentence."
Another is to be kind to yourself. Studies have found that students who forgave themselves for procrastinating were less likely to do it again.
So next time you catch yourself scrolling instead of studying, don't beat yourself up. Just pick one tiny step and start.
That's it for today. Catch you next week!
